title: QPortfolio Model
description: Root document for a QPortfolio model file (qp_file_type = "QPortfolio Model"): a portfolio's metrics and attribute definitions. Metric and attribute names must match the names used in the portfolio's data file exactly. Both sections are optional.

metadata.description: Document header. For a model file qp_file_type must be "QPortfolio Model".

qp_file_type.description: Discriminator for the document type: "QPortfolio Data" for a portfolio data file, "QPortfolio Scenario Data" for a scenario file, "QPortfolio Model" for a model file and "QPortfolio Bundle" for a bundle manifest. Required.

qp_version.description: Version of the QPortfolio application that wrote this file, e.g. 4.6. Optional; when omitted the importer assumes the current version. A version newer than the importing application's is refused.

metrics.description: The metrics of the model — the variables it reads or computes. metric_name must be unique across the file. Optional; an empty list is valid.

items.description: A metric: a variable in the model, either imported (input and master data; no expressions) or computed by its expressions.

metric_name.description: Unique case-insensitive name of the metric, e.g. "Capex-Drilling". Must match the name used for this metric in the portfolio data file. Braces { } are not allowed (they delimit references inside expression formulas). Names ending in "#<Type>" for a derivation type (see derived) are reserved for derived metrics, unconditionally and whatever the metric's type: a metric named "Revenue#CumSum" is rejected at import — list the derivation type under the origin metric's derived instead.

metric_type.description: The type of metric (input, master data, or computed). A metric with expressions must be Computed. When re-importing into a model that already defines this metric, its type cannot switch between input and computed (rejected at import). Allowed values: `Input` — An input metric whose values are imported per opportunity.; `MasterData` — A master-data metric: a value that applies across all opportunities (e.g. a price deck, FX, inflation) and is matched to each via attributes.; `Computed` — A computed metric, calculated from other metrics by its expressions..

scalar.description: When true this metric is a scalar: a single value rather than the default per-period time series (an indicator). Optional; defaults to false.

hidden.description: When true this metric is hidden — an interim sub-metric produced when a compound expression is broken into intermediate parts. Optional; defaults to false. A metric already imported as visible cannot be switched to hidden on a later import (rejected at import).

level.description: The calculation level of the metric — where a computed metric's expressions are calculated. Required on every metric, inputs and master data included. Allowed values: `Outcome` — Calculated per opportunity-outcome pair (the lowest level); outcome weights then produce the expected value.; `Scenario` — Calculated for the whole scenario with inputs aggregated across all opportunities (e.g. a graduated tax).; `Group` — Calculated per group of opportunities aggregated by an attribute (see group_by) for ring-fenced, entity-by-entity calculations.; `Opportunity` — Calculated from each opportunity's expected values; usually matches Outcome with faster run time..

group_by.description: For a Group-level metric, the attribute name(s) whose values define the groups, e.g. ["Country"] or ["Country", "Region"] for multi-level grouping. Required when level is Group; used only then.

scale_by.description: How the metric value is scaled for a selection of an opportunity. Optional; defaults to Interest. Allowed values: `Interest` — Scaled by the fractional selected interest (the default).; `Instance` — Scaled by the number of selected instances..

expressions.description: The expressions that compute this metric, in Excel-style formula syntax. Only computed metrics have any. Missing, null and [] all mean none, and a computed metric with none computes 0. Each is optionally restricted by criteria, and the one with the LOWEST order whose criteria match is the one used. An expression with no criteria matches everything, so it shadows every higher order: an exception needs a LOWER order than the unfiltered default, not a higher one.

items.description: One expression that computes a metric. The formula is written in Excel-style syntax; references to other metrics and attributes are wrapped in ${...}, e.g. "${Opex - Fixed} + ${Opex - Variable}" or "CumSum(${Revenue})". Special functions (Disc, CumSum, Total, GetMetricValue, GetAttributeValue, …), operators and numeric constants are written bare. Macro functions (e.g. FlagUpToMax) are not supported in JSON model files (rejected at import).

order.description: Evaluation order of this expression among the metric's expressions: the LOWEST order whose criteria match is the one used, so an exception needs a lower order than the unfiltered default. Required, and different on every expression of the metric.

criteria.description: Filters restricting which opportunities, outcomes, groups or periods this expression applies to. Omit or leave empty for an unfiltered (default) expression. Multiple criteria combine as OR.

items.description: A single filter on an expression. Any combination of attribute/characteristic, opportunity, outcome and time period may be set; each condition accepts one or more values (the expression applies when the outcome matches any of them), and each may be negated with its corresponding except_* flag (apply everywhere except the named values). A filter whose attribute or characteristic was deleted exports as "#Missing".

attribute.description: Attribute name to filter by (use together with characteristic). Optional; omit it rather than writing an empty name.

characteristic.description: Characteristic values of the attribute to filter by. Optional.

opportunity.description: Opportunity names to filter by. Optional.

outcome.description: Outcome names to filter by, e.g. "Fail". Optional.

period.description: Time periods (0-based) this expression applies to. Optional.

except_attribute.description: When true the attribute/characteristic filter is negated (apply except to the named characteristics). Optional; defaults to false.

except_opportunity.description: When true the opportunity filter is negated. Optional; defaults to false.

except_outcome.description: When true the outcome filter is negated. Optional; defaults to false.

except_period.description: When true the time period filter is negated. Optional; defaults to false.

formula.description: The formula evaluated for each time period. Every metric/attribute reference is wrapped in ${...} (the name inside must match a defined metric/attribute exactly). References are resolved, and the formula's syntax, functions and argument counts are validated, when the file is imported (cross-metric checks the schema itself cannot express).

first_period_formula.description: Optional formula that seeds the first time period only (e.g. an opening balance); formula governs subsequent periods. Omit when the first period uses the same formula - do not write an empty string.

unit.description: Unit label for the metric, e.g. "$ MM", "bbl/d". QPortfolio only labels and verifies unit consistency; it does not convert units. "", missing or null = no unit.

format.description: Numeric display format for the metric on dashboard widgets. NOT a format pattern — "0.00" is stored and then ignored. It is a JSON OBJECT serialized into this string, every member optional: {"style": 0 decimal | 1 currency | 2 percent, "currencyDisplay": 0 symbol | 1 name, "minimumIntegerDigits": n, "minimumFractionDigits": n, "maximumFractionDigits": n, "useGrouping": true | false}. E.g. "{\"style\":0,\"minimumFractionDigits\":2,\"maximumFractionDigits\":2,\"useGrouping\":true}" renders 1,234.00. Optional.

color.description: Display colour for the metric on dashboard widgets, as a hex string, e.g. "#1F77B4". Optional; unset, the metric reads back with a generated colour.

category.description: Optional category the metric is grouped under.

description.description: Free-text description of the metric. Optional.

derived.description: Derivation types to generate from this metric; each yields a metric named "<this metric's name>#<Type>", e.g. ["CumSum"] on Revenue yields "Revenue#CumSum". Optional.

items.description: A derivation type: the transform applied to an origin metric to produce a derived metric. Discounting and inflation use the portfolio's rates. Allowed values: `PT` — Previous Time: the origin's value one time period earlier.; `Disc` — Discounted: the origin's per-period value discounted to the start.; `Inf` — Inflated: the origin's per-period value with inflation applied.; `CumSum` — Running Cumulative: the origin summed from the first period up to each period.; `CumSumDisc` — Running Cumulative Discounted: like CumSum, over discounted values.; `CumSumInf` — Running Cumulative Inflated: like CumSum, over inflated values.; `Total` — Total: the origin summed over all time periods — a scalar.; `TotalDisc` — Total Discounted: the discounted origin summed over all time periods — a scalar.; `TotalInf` — Total Inflated: the inflated origin summed over all time periods — a scalar.; `MaxAT` — Max All Time: the origin's largest value across all time periods — a scalar..

attributes.description: Attribute definitions and their allowed characteristics (data type, scenario-level, editability, and each characteristic's display order and colour). The per-opportunity characteristic values live in the portfolio data file; the two are joined by attribute/characteristic name. Optional.

items.description: An attribute definition: a grouping category (e.g. Country, Project Type) together with its data type and its allowed characteristics.

attribute_name.description: Unique name of the attribute, e.g. "Country". Must match the name used in the portfolio data file. Braces { } are not allowed (they delimit references inside expression formulas).

data_type.description: Data type of the attribute's characteristics. Allowed values: `String` — Text characteristics, e.g. Country = Canada.; `Numeric` — Numeric characteristics.; `Date` — Date characteristics..

scenario_level.description: When true the attribute's characteristic can be selected at scenario level (e.g. a price set) for sensitivity analysis. Optional; unset is false for a new attribute and keeps an existing attribute's value.

editable.description: When true the attribute's characteristic values on opportunities are user-editable. Optional; defaults to false.

characteristics.description: The known characteristic values for this attribute, with their display order and colour.

items.description: A characteristic definition: one known value of an attribute, with its display ordering and colour (used when charts render this characteristic).

characteristic_name.description: The characteristic value, e.g. "Canada". A Date attribute's value is an Excel serial-date number as text, e.g. "45322" = 2024-01-31; a Numeric attribute's is a plain number as text.

sort_order.description: Sort order of this characteristic within its attribute (lower first). Optional.

color.description: Display colour for this characteristic on charts, as a hex string, e.g. "#1F77B4". Optional.
